[A825] TAKEN
Branch: pf-977-1 (from dd163e41, PR #960's reviewed head; the PR's base is dev-soft-core)
Authoritative references: #977 (acceptance: the ruling of 2026-11-22); #969's measurement (issuecomment-7083505751); #665; #872 (the indexed lookup); IEEE 802.1Q-2018 10.7 (the MRP state machines, Join and LeaveAll timing) and 35.2 (MSRP's Talker attributes); Milan v1.2 4.2.7 and 5.3.8; docs/design/SPLIT_CONTROL_MEMORY.md section 13; tb/verilator/ctrl_service_budget.
Interpreted scope: Profile, by function, the ~16k CPU cycles lwSRP and the SRP adapter spend per registered Talker on the split CPU at 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if, on the built images. Add a CPU budget harness group that drives the fastest registering burst the MRP state machines allow (every input's Talker registered, and re-declared after a LeaveAll) on top of the every-source flood, and read the owner rows (last notice, ACMP, txL, the loads) directly. Make registration its own term (count x cost) in load_grade, the SRP unit unchanged. Apply the lever the profile names: if attribute lookup dominates, the indexed lookup (lwSRP's buckets on the attribute key) set for 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if through an lwSRP change of its own with its own reviews; otherwise the cheaper exact change. Show an every-input registering record within its slice (950 us at 1x1/1if, 1,475 us at 8x8/1if), every owner bound unmoved, and behaviour identical (frames and registrar state) on every harness arm, with planted defects. No change to the CPU budget's approved limits, the mailbox contract or RTL.
Validation plan: the per-function profile at both points; the new group and its grader with planted controls; the firmware gate (four shards); the two-placement twin and its plants; the CPU budget rows and graders (flip_grade, load_grade, shape_costs) at 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if; the memory ledger (plat_ledger, test_ctrl_memory); routes at 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if if the images change; the docs workflow.

Branch `pf-977-1` (from `dd163e41`, PR #960's reviewed head): 2 local commits, not pushed. They hold the measurement only: two CPU budget harness groups (`register_window.py`) and their README paragraph. Nothing is changed toward any option. The receipts (profiles, runs, tables, the lever candidates as patches) are in round 1's packet for the manager.

**1. The profile.** The registering record is one MRPDU declaring every input's Talker Advertise, every input bound first (`srp-register`), traced by committed PC from `apply_receive`. Each cycle is charged to the function of its last committed PC; inclusive cycles come from the rebuilt call stack.

| Point | Base | Buckets (candidate 1) | Candidate 2 | Candidate 3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1x1/1if, 2 Talkers | 38,155 cycles | 37,835 | 37,364 | 31,325 |
| 8x8/1if, 9 Talkers | 140,329 | 119,970 | 112,897 | 92,280 |

- At 8x8/1if no function dominates. Per Talker, inclusive, at base:
  - event delivery 4.6k (`reg_event`'s map-work calloc and free, the indication, the observer);
  - lookup 2.5k (`find_attr` twice a Talker, `msrp_attr_cmp`, `memcmp`);
  - creation 2.5k (a calloc and its zeroing);
  - the two parse passes' decode 1.8k;
  - the adapter's receive filter 1.5k;
  - the snapshots 1.4k.
- Lookup is lwSRP's largest family, 16 % of the record. Copies (`forward` 14.0k), zeroing (`memset` 11.1k) and the adapter's sink loops (`same`, 225 calls, 12.5k) are as large.
- At 1x1/1if lookup is 1.1k of 38k, and the buckets move nothing.
- The record's pass carries ACMP's reaction in its polls. `ctrl_app_srp`'s delivery calls `acmp_tk_registered` for each sink, and the ACMP core's completion runs: about 5k cycles a registration, 45 to 55k at 8x8/1if.
  - At base that pass is 211,080 cycles, over THE SHARE, and its polls' base is 65,301 against 30,000 stated.
  - THE TRANSMIT's build after it is 165,639 against the 147,500 slice: the nine Listener declarations re-declared Ready, their VLAN joins, and the MRPDU, whose vector sort is 38.6k of `memcmp`.
- **A record that replaces every input's Talker** (Advertise for Failed or back; IEEE 802.1Q-2018 35.2.6, Milan v1.2 4.2.7.2.2) costs 19.7k cycles a Talker on candidate 2. Each Talker takes three deliveries: the old kind's rapid leave, its leave timer, and the new kind's JoinIn.
  - Two map-work alloc, copy and free pairs: about 27k of the record.
  - 108 value copies: 24k.
  - Both indications through `talker_changed`: 16.8k.

**2. The measurement (`srp-register-burst`).**
- Every input is bound first. Then three triples of MRPDUs arrive on every receive channel's flood at its contract rate.
- A peer transmits at most three MRPDUs in any 1.5 x JoinTime (IEEE 802.1Q-2018 10.7.11), and JoinTime is at least 180 ms (Milan v1.2 Table 4.3), so the triples are at least 270 ms apart.
- Each MRPDU declares every input's Talker JoinIn, the kinds alternating, so every record registers every input anew. The last triple opens with the peer's LeaveAll on the registered kind and its re-declaration.
- Each triple arrives 1 ms ahead of an ACMP flood burst.

| Candidate | Point | Dearest record | Longest SRP slice | Longest build | Passes over THE SHARE (longest) | Late MRP timer run-outs | ACMP last record | AECP last record | Our MRPDU (JoinTime wait) | Probe misses |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| base | 1x1/1if | 54,617 | 102,077 | 63,456 | 0 | 0 | 3.78 ms | 3.07 ms | 156.83 ms | 0 of 15 |
| base | 8x8/1if | 255,420 | 322,427 | 263,318 | 11 (388,518) | 2 (101 ms, against 49) | 5.68 ms | 2.47 ms | 155.01 ms | 0 of 15 |
| buckets | 1x1/1if | 53,977 | 115,056 | 62,438 | 0 | 0 | 3.98 ms | 3.19 ms | 154.94 ms | 0 of 15 |
| buckets | 8x8/1if | 193,537 | 276,434 | 256,776 | 10 (343,062) | 0 | 6.17 ms | 4.55 ms | 160.98 ms | 0 of 15 |
| candidate 2 | 1x1/1if | 52,408 | 99,956 | 76,013 | 0 | 0 | 3.83 ms | 3.19 ms | 155.97 ms | 0 of 15 |
| candidate 2 | 8x8/1if | 179,321 | 258,788 | 217,715 | 8 (325,373) | 0 | 5.97 ms | 4.40 ms | 160.81 ms | 0 of 15 |
| candidate 3 | 1x1/1if | 44,112 | 85,099 | 78,552 | 0 | 0 | 1.77 ms | 3.51 ms | 156.22 ms | 0 of 15 |
| candidate 3 | 8x8/1if | 139,691 | 224,475 | 215,082 | 9 (297,413) | 0 | 5.52 ms | 3.83 ms | 160.55 ms | 0 of 15 |

The figures in the first four numeric columns are CPU cycles. The stated slice is 95,000 cycles at 1x1/1if and 147,500 at 8x8/1if.

- **The rows read directly hold** at both points within the harness's budgets (T_svc or less, plus a JoinTime's wait for our MRPDU): ACMP's and AECP's last record of their burst behind each triple, each registering record to its pass's end, and our MRPDU.
- **At 1x1/1if** every record fits its 950 us slice and no pass is over THE SHARE. The model's statements are what is over: a registering record's apply over the unit, the registrar walk after it, and (base to candidate 2) a slice that starts a registering record with only the unit left.
- **At 8x8/1if**, under base and candidates 1 and 2, a replacing record is past the 1,475 us slice. Under candidate 3 every record fits it (139,691 of 147,500). Under every candidate:
  - passes are over THE SHARE. The drain starts a record whenever the unit's 375 us is left, so it takes two registering records into one slice (224,475 on candidate 3). A record's pass also carries ACMP's delivery of the swapped kinds.
  - THE TRANSMIT's builds after the swaps are past the slice (215,082 on candidate 3).
- At base two MRP timers' run-outs (the periodic and the join timer) found our first frame 101 ms after their transmit opportunity, past THE TRANSMIT's 49 ms.

**3. The model.** A registration is its own term (count x cost), and the SRP unit is unchanged. The cost is a Talker's share of its record's excess over the unit plus ACMP's delivery of it, the dearest over both groups, stated by the load gate's rule.

| 8x8/1if load at the pin's column (today 0.74357, ceiling 0.75) | Base (310 us) | Buckets (240 us) | Candidate 2 (220 us) | Candidate 3 (175 us) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (a) count at the MRP state machines' rate: every input's Talker in each of three MRPDUs a 1.5 x 180 ms, 0.1 a ms | 0.7746 | 0.7676 | 0.7656 | 0.7611 |
| (b) count at LeaveAll timing: every input's Talker once a 9.5 s leavealltimer (Milan v1.2 Table 4.3) | 0.7439 | 0.7438 | 0.7438 | 0.7437 |

- 1x1/1if is within its 0.70 under both counts at every candidate: 0.5157 at the worst.
- (a) is the load gate's own rule: an arrival bound from a protocol timer, here the transmit opportunity's. A peer whose streams swap kinds at each transmit opportunity is legal under MRP. Holding 0.75 under (a) needs about 64 us a Talker all-in at 8x8/1if, against candidate 3's 175: ACMP's delivery alone is about 50.
- (b) does not bound such a peer.

**4. The levers measured.** These are scratch candidates; nothing is committed.
- **Candidate 1:** lwSRP at opt-exec-1 (343c610), `LWSRP_ATTR_BUCKETS=16u` on the one-interface images.
  - At 8x8/1if it cuts a registering record 15 % and a replacing record about 25 %, since lwSRP's replacement scan of the whole list goes.
  - It removes the base's pass over THE SHARE in `srp-register`.
- **Candidate 2:** candidate 1 plus `LWSRP_TX_MERGE=1` and two adapter cuts, exact by construction. One is a byte compare before `same` in the sink loops. The other is the receive filter taking only the sinks a Talker indication touched. It gains 6 % more.
  - The merged build regresses 1x1/1if: the longest `build_mrpdu` is 43,815 cycles against 33,927, and a build pass is 76,013 against the 73,500 stated.
  - Its 8x8/1if size fixture plans 56.5 RAMB36 (rom 131,336 B), which would be recorded S14 debt.
- **Candidate 3:** candidate 2 plus two lwSRP changes, on a scratch lwSRP commit.
  - No map-work reservation and no policy call where the participant has one port. The reservation is a calloc, copy and free per indication, kept for a port lwSRP's MSRP policy never names: every one of its answers excludes the source port, and MVRP and MMRP have no policy. This is exact except where that allocation would have been refused, which it now never is.
  - No zeroing of each decoded value in the validation pass, which is exact.
  - At 8x8/1if a replacing record drops 22 to 25 % (125k to 140k of 147,500) and the registering record 18 % (92,280).
- **What is left:**
  - The ACMP core's per-sink completion in tsn-c-stack: 45 to 55k cycles in the record's pass.
  - The drain's admission, which charges every record at the unit.
  - THE TRANSMIT's builds after the swaps (215k), which re-declare every Listener, join their VLANs and sort the MRPDU.

**Decision requested** (no change made toward any option):
1. What does the bound hold at 8x8/1if under the burst?
   - Each record within its slice: candidate 3 meets that. It needs an lwSRP PR beyond opt-exec-1 for the one-port map work.
   - THE SHARE and THE TRANSMIT's build slice as well: these need more than this lane's levers. The drain would charge a record by the Talkers it carries, which changes the firmware's admission and so needs a ruling of its own. The ACMP core's per-sink completion (tsn-c-stack) and the builds after a swap would need cutting. Otherwise 8x8/1if is held as the owner decides.
2. The registration term's count: (a) the MRP state machines' rate, or (b) LeaveAll timing.
   - Under (a) the 8x8/1if load is over 0.75 at every lever measured.
   - Under (b) it holds at every candidate.

[A10] Ruling on the round-1 STOP (owner-delegated decision, 2026-11-23; nothing goes to the owner now).

1. **The registration term counts at the MRP state machines' rate (option a).**
   - IEEE 802.1Q-2018 10.7.11 bounds MRPDUs, not attribute changes.
   - LeaveTime limits only same-kind re-registration: a registrar in LV returns to IN with no new indication.
   - A kind replacement (35.2.6; Milan v1.2 4.2.7.2.2) is immediate, so a legal peer can swap every Talker at each transmit opportunity.
   - No clause gives a lower sustained rate; LeaveAll timing describes a quiet network, not a bound.
   - **Target:** 64 us a Talker, all-in, at 8x8/1if.
2. **The bound:** each record within its slice is not enough; THE SHARE and THE TRANSMIT's build slice must hold under the burst too.
   - THE SHARE is the premise of the 140 ms and 49 ms rows.
   - At the base the mechanism is visible: the first frame at 101 ms, 52 ms past THE TRANSMIT.
3. **Round 2, review-ready by 11-25:**
   - an lwSRP PR beyond opt-exec-1: the buckets, one-port map work, and no validation zeroing, with the refused-allocation difference documented;
   - both adapter cuts;
   - Talker indications marked per sink in the record's pass; ACMP completion and the Listener re-declaration run from the latest kind in their own slices;
   - the transmit merge off at 1x1/1if.
4. **The drain ruling: approved.**
   - A record is charged the unit plus the registration cost times the Talker values it can carry.
   - The count comes from a bound read before parsing, never under it.
   - A record alone in a slice always starts; order is kept and nothing is dropped.
   - The burst group gates the wait within T_svc.
5. **Round 3, by 11-27:** the builds after swaps (sort, re-declares), the copies and zeroing, and a single-delivery replacement, until 64 us is met.
6. **Escalation:** only if on 11-27 the option-(a) load is still over 0.75, or passes exceed THE SHARE, does it go to the owner. The question would be whether 8x8/1if goes to the lab with the swap-rate load over by at most 0.012, as first debt after.

**2. Why 64 us is not reached.** On the head's image a registering record costs 13,877 CPU cycles a Talker all in at 8x8/1if (150 us by the rule): 8,629 its share of the record past the unit (95 us) and 5,444 its share of THE SETTLE after it (60 us). At 1x1/1if it is 12,508 (135 us). THE SETTLE is ACMP's completion of each sink the record changed, in tsn-c-stack, outside item 5's list, so even a record that cost nothing past the unit would leave about 60 us. Round 3's exact cuts took the all-in cost from round 2's 17,598 to 13,877 cycles a Talker: lwSRP's rapid replacement, lean copies and lean tx!, the reversed descending Message, the sink index, the walk owed only for a source's StreamID. A replacement in one delivery would change the Mt vectors MRP sends, so it is not taken. Without the term the load is 0.744. The flip check reads the pin's column, which states the five costs of ACMP's completion walk at the larger of their measurements before and after tsn-c-stack #32 (a statement never goes down). At the measurements of images carrying #32 alone (load_grade's donor column) the load is 0.719. Neither is mine to change.
